title: Fixing a variable lowers the free count by at most one
statement: Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, let $v$ be one of these variables, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. Let $\rho'$ be the restriction that fixes $v$ to $b$ and agrees with $\rho$ on every other variable. Writing $f(\sigma)$ for the number of free variables of a restriction $\sigma$, we have $f(\rho') + 1 \ge f(\rho)$; that is, fixing a single variable reduces the number of free variables by at most one.
hypotheses_covered: ρ is a restriction on n variables
ρ' fixes v to b and agrees with ρ elsewhere
replaced:
Updating $\rho$ at $v$ to $\mathrm{some}\,b$ decreases $\mathrm{numFree}$ by at
most one: $\mathrm{numFree}(\rho[v \mapsto b]) + 1 \geq \rho.\mathrm{numFree}$.
